title: Security posture discovery with Novus Insurance
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate
Share VPC/private deployment diagram and onboarding checklist
Schedule compliance deep dive with security engineering (week of 2027-05-10)
Provide initial pricing for Dedicated capacity and BYOK options
action_items: Samir Patel: Send SOC2 report and security whitepaper (due 2027-05-05)
Jules Park: Prepare network diagram for VPC/private deployment (due 2027-05-07)
Maya Thompson: Provide data residency requirements and list of regulated data types (due 2027-05-06)
topics: Encryption at rest / BYOK / KMS / HSM
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Novus Insurance evaluating Redwood for underwriting document automation. Main concerns: SOC 2 / ISO attestation, SSO/SAML + SCIM, strict RBAC, audit logs and retention for regulatory audits, encryption/BYOK, and data residency. Novus leaning toward Dedicated or Private for PII ingestion but open to a Hosted pilot with strong contractual controls.
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-05-03 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Redwood: Samir Patel (AE), Jules Park (SE)
Novus Insurance: Maya Thompson (CISO), Eric Li (Head of Platform), Sofia Ramos (Eng Manager)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Jules our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Thompson: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:10] Jules Park: Hi Maya, Eric, Sofia. We'll focus on security posture and the questions you sent over. We'll try to cover hosted vs dedicated vs private options and the controls around encryption, SSO, logging and retention.
[00:22] Eric Li: Great — high level first: we ingest underwriting docs that contain PII and some regulated financial data. Our legal/compliance team wants to understand whether Redwood Hosted is acceptable or we need Dedicated/Private.
[00:34] Samir Patel: Totally. High level, many customers start on Redwood Hosted for rapid iteration but for regulated data you typically evaluate Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and data isolation; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives the tightest network controls.
[00:48] Maya Thompson: Our checklist: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 are musts, SSO (SAML + SCIM), fine-grained RBAC, immutable audit logs with exports, encryption in-transit and at-rest, BYOK with HSM preferred, and retention/deletion controls. Also data residency — we need EU-only for a subset of data.
[01:07] Jules Park: Understood. On SOC2/ISO: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing/has ISO27001 — we can share the reports under NDA. I will attach the latest SOC2 report and our security whitepaper after this call.
[01:20] Maya Thompson: Good. On BYOK — does Redwood allow customer-managed keys for both Hosted and Dedicated? Does that rely on cloud KMS or can you integrate with our HSM?
[01:30] Jules Park: Short answer: we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private through cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we have an HSM integration path for Private/on-prem. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest with our keys and offer contractual assurances; BYOK on Hosted is possible for enterprise deals but has some constraints — we should flag that as an action item to scope with engineering.
[01:52] Eric Li: Can you confirm whether logs and the audit trail are tamper-evident? We need to show chain-of-custody for requests and responses for audits.
[02:03] Jules Park: We maintain audit logs for control plane and tenant activity. Logs include request metadata, model used, token counts, and route decisions. For Dedicated/Private deployments logs can be shipped to a customer-owned SIEM via TLS and we support immutable storage patterns (WORM) on request. For Hosted we provide audit exports and long-term retention add-ons.
[02:27] Sofia Ramos: What's the default retention window for logs and for content? Our policy requires 7 years retention for some artifacts.
[02:34] Samir Patel: Default retention on Hosted is 90 days for full transcripts, with aggregated metrics retained longer. We have compliance add-ons for extended retention and archival export. For Dedicated/Private you control retention fully — you can push to your S3 bucket or on-prem archive. We'll send the retention guide.
[02:50] Maya Thompson: About SSO and provisioning: we'd need SCIM to push groups and role mappings. How granular is RBAC?
[02:57] Jules Park: We support SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC allows role-level permissions (admin, developer, viewer) and route/model-level controls. For stricter needs we can support attribute-based access or integrate with your ABAC policy engine when in Private mode.
[03:14] Eric Li: Any encryption-in-transit cert requirements? We run strict mTLS between our services — can Redwood support mutual TLS for API calls?
[03:22] Jules Park: We support TLS 1.2+ for all endpoints. mTLS for API is available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we use standard TLS with client API keys; mutual TLS can be evaluated for enterprise contracts.
[03:37] Maya Thompson: Data residency — we need to ensure that EU data never leaves EU. Does Redwood have region-restricted hosting?
[03:45] Samir Patel: Yes, we support region pinning for model serving and storage. Hosted offers region options in EU and US; Dedicated can be provisioned in the region of your choice; Private obviously runs in your VPC/region. We'll include a diagram of region routing and our data flow.
[03:59] Sofia Ramos: Pen tests and vulnerability disclosure — do you run regular pentests and provide reports?
[04:05] Jules Park: We run annual third-party pen tests and triage tickets. We also have a vulnerability disclosure policy and will share the summary report and timelines under NDA.
[04:16] Eric Li: For our proof-of-concept, we'd like to run small-scale inference on real data. If we start on Hosted, what's the SLA for data deletion after a run, and can we ensure no data is cached/shared?
[04:28] Samir Patel: On Hosted we have configurable prefix/KV caching; by default we don't persist payloads beyond the retention window, but we can put a contractual clause for non-persistent handling for pilot data. For Dedicated/Private, you control caches entirely — no multi-tenant cache. We'll provide a pilot playbook.
[04:45] Maya Thompson: Regarding model artifacts — if you do model fine-tuning or caching of embeddings, how is that handled?
[04:51] Jules Park: Fine-tuning on Hosted is gated; we generally recommend Dedicated or Private for persistent model builds with PII due to traceability concerns. Embeddings and KV cache can be encrypted and are stored per-tenant in Dedicated/Private.
[05:05] Eric Li: Is there a straightforward way to get SOC2 Type II report and any recent ISO certification? We need to share with legal.
[05:12] Samir Patel: Yes — I'll send the SOC2 Type II report and our security whitepaper today. Jules will attach the ISO evidence and the pen test summary. We'll put them behind the NDA link.
[05:20] Maya Thompson: One more — do you support SAML attributes for project-level scopes? We map SAML groups to model access in our RBAC.
[05:29] Jules Park: Yes, SAML attributes can be mapped to roles; SCIM can provision groups. In Private we can extend mappings to project-level scoping.
[05:36] Sofia Ramos: Any network requirements for VPC peering? Our infra team needs inbound/outbound diagrams.
[05:43] Samir Patel: We'll provide a VPC peering diagram and a checklist of firewall rules, NAT and endpoint policies. Jules will own that artifact.
[05:52] Maya Thompson: On legal — we need data processing addendum and commitments around breach notification times. What's Redwood's standard?
[05:59] Samir Patel: Standard is 72-hour breach notification; we can discuss shorter windows in enterprise terms. We have a data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses; legal can provide redlines.
[06:12] Eric Li: Are there any limitations around model variants or quantized model execution that affect reproducibility of outputs for audit purposes?
[06:21] Jules Park: We surface model versioning and inference profiles. For compliance we can pin model versions and maintain determinism checks (seeded sampling options) and log the model variant used per request. Quantization shouldn't affect deterministic logging but we can document any variance.
[06:37] Maya Thompson: OK. Budget and procurement note: if Dedicated/Private is required we will need a capital decision and procurement timeline of ~8-12 weeks. Pilot on Hosted reduces that risk but we need legal sign-off.
[06:50] Samir Patel: Makes sense. We'll aim to support a Hosted pilot with contractual protections while you evaluate Dedicated/Private for production.
[06:58] Eric Li: About BYOK — any limits on key rotation or number of keys per tenant?
[07:04] Jules Park: We support standard KMS rotation schedules; for HSM/BYOK we coordinate rotation via API calls. There are practical limits we can share in the BYOK spec.
[07:14] Maya Thompson: Let's capture next steps.
[07:17] Samir Patel: Yep — recap: Samir to send SOC2 and security whitepaper, Jules to send VPC diagram and BYOK spec, and schedule a compliance deep-dive next week. Maya to send a short data residency/PII inventory.
[07:28] Maya Thompson: That works. Thanks.
[07:30] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:33] [Call ends]
